high.title: IPCA Rises More Than Expected in May and Accumulates 4.72% Rise, Above Target
high.summary: Brazil's official inflation rate (IPCA) rose 0.58% in May, above market expectations of 0.55%, according to IBGE data. While this represents a deceleration from April's 0.67%, the 12-month accumulated inflation reached 4.72%, exceeding the Central Bank's 3% target and breaking through the 4.5% ceiling of the tolerance band. Market consensus had expected 4.68% for the 12-month period. The main drivers were Food and beverages (+1.33%, contributing 0.29 p.p.), Housing (+1.22%, contributing 0.18 p.p.), and Health and personal care. This above-target inflation strengthens the case for the Central Bank to maintain or potentially raise the Selic rate at upcoming COPOM meetings. For BRL traders, this creates a hawkish bias that could support the Real against USD, while bond yields may face upward pressure as markets price in tighter monetary policy. The data reinforces concerns about persistent inflationary pressures despite economic uncertainties.

high.title: Ibovespa Reverses Signal and Rises with IPCA Above Ceiling and US-Iran Agreement in Focus; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (12)
high.summary: The Ibovespa opened negative after inflation came above expectations and breached the Central Bank's target ceiling, but quickly reversed to positive territory. By 10:20 AM, the index was up 0.14% at 171,718.44 points after initially falling 0.60%. USD/BRL was trading higher at R$ 5.1055 (+0.08%) while the DXY fell 0.02%. The market is closely watching potential US-Iran negotiations with a possible memorandum of understanding to be signed over the weekend. This geopolitical development, combined with above-target IPCA inflation creating expectations for tighter monetary policy, is creating mixed signals for Brazilian assets.

high.title: Treasury Direct Today: Rates Fall at Opening Despite IPCA Above Expected; Understand
high.summary: Brazilian government bond yields opened lower despite May IPCA coming above expectations, driven by relief over Middle East geopolitical tensions. The Treasury Prefixed 2029 fell from 14.60% to 14.53%, while IPCA+ 2050 dropped from IPCA + 7.20% to IPCA + 7.06%, and IPCA+ 2040 declined from IPCA + 7.51% to IPCA + 7.35%. Risk appetite improved after President Trump decided against further attacks on Iran, with a potential US-Iran memorandum of understanding expected by Sunday that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days, reducing oil supply concerns.

medium.title: Ibovespa Rises with Improved Investor Sentiment and Returns to Test 169 Thousand Points; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (11)
medium.summary: The Ibovespa followed improved risk sentiment abroad amid new Middle East developments, with US pressure for a definitive peace agreement. By 10:10 AM, the index was up 0.19% at 168,939 points. USD/BRL fell to R$ 5.1640 (-0.17%) while DXY rose 0.12%. Brazil's service volume registered above-expected growth in April at 1.2% month-over-month, above Reuters consensus of 0.6%, recovering from a weak first quarter.

medium.title: For the First Time in 3 Years, ECB Raises Interest Rates to Contain War-Caused Inflation
medium.summary: The European Central Bank raised interest rates for the first time in almost three years, hoping to contain inflation before energy cost increases from the Iran war spread more widely through the eurozone economy. Eurozone inflation is already above 3%, well above the ECB's 2% target, while economic growth remains very weak. This international monetary tightening trend could influence global capital flows and provide context for Brazil's monetary policy decisions.
